summary: The fetch is split in two and the PR-head half no longer names a branch. Invocation one (:181) is `$TIP` plus the `+refs/heads/lane/*` wildcard and contains no name that can be missing, so it cannot fail the way pass 1 demonstrated; invocation two (:189) fetches `+refs/pull/<n>/head:refs/remotes/pr/<n>`, which GitHub publishes for every open PR including a fork's and including one whose head branch was deleted, and the PR number is validated as a number (:186) before it is interpolated into a ref path. A failed batch retries one spec at a time (:195-206) so one bad pull ref costs its own PR head only. The destination namespace is `refs/remotes/pr/`, checked inert to every other job: no reader outside arms.sh walks anything but refs/remotes/origin/ (fold.sh:231, cloud.sh:377, lane.sh:212, bootstrap-board-branch.sh:15), so a fork PR whose head is named `board` can no longer overwrite the ref the board is read from.
scenario: Pass 1's scenario -- one open PR from a fork, or one open PR whose head branch was deleted, aborting the whole `git fetch` so that nothing updates at all and every prediction pushed thereafter on master or any lane branch is invisible to the queue for as long as that PR stays open -- can no longer occur: the trunk and lane/* are already updated before any name that can be missing is asked for.
evidence: Measured, not read. 98-lane-shape.sh:129-217 builds a real bare origin with two open PRs -- #777 (head present, published at refs/pull/777/head) and #778 (`vanished-head`, on that origin neither as a branch nor as a pull ref) -- and pushes a prediction to master after the consumer's last fetch. On this tip the tick advances refs/remotes/origin/master to the pushed sha (:205), collects master:docs/testing/predictions/trunk.json (:207), names `PR head unavailable ... refs/pull/778/head` (:211) and has fetched refs/remotes/pr/777 (:216); the fixture's own precondition leg (:202) asserts the consumer was behind before the tick, so those are not green for a fetch that did nothing. I ran this branch's fragment against the pre-remediation tip 8b185a925f in a scratch worktree (runner byte-identical, diff -q): :205, :207, :211 and :216 all FAIL there. Against master@11ddd94a66 they pass, correctly -- master fetches no PR heads at all, so H1 was a defect this branch introduced and master is the wrong falsifier for it; NOTES.md:437-446 says exactly that.
